_about: The email templates of the American Playbook. `playbook.py template` renders them. A slot the founder has not filled stays as a [bracket] and is reported as a missing fact: the engine never fills a metric, a logo or a name on its own. `example` holds the illustrative filled version from the guide; it is shown in the references and never used as output.
group_count_note: The guide counts 12 template groups: cold, conference follow-up, forwardable intro, recap, value bump, second angle, breakup, re-entry, monthly investor update, bar-extraction reply, thank-you and loop-close, LinkedIn and scheduling.

templates.title: Cold outreach (the base template)
templates.when: First contact, ideally with a connector or a specific trigger in the first line.
templates.subject: Intro via [Connector] - [the outcome, 3-5 words]
templates.body:
Hi [First name],

[Connector] mentioned [what they are working on].

We help [ICP] [outcome + number] - [one proof point].

Worth a 20-minute call to see if this is relevant for [their plan or timeframe]? Happy to work around your calendar.

Best,
[Founder]
templates.notes: No connector? Replace the first line with the specific trigger you noticed, and drop "Intro via" from the subject.
templates.example:
Subject: Intro via Sarah - cutting claims processing time

Hi Michael,

Sarah Cohen mentioned you're rebuilding the claims workflow at Acme.

We help mid-size insurers cut claims processing time by about 40% - we're already running paid pilots with two carriers.

Worth a 20-minute call to see if this is relevant for your Q1 plans? Happy to work around your calendar.

Best,
Dana

templates.title: Conference / event follow-up (they said "send me something")
templates.when: After meeting someone at an event who asked you to send something.
templates.subject: Great meeting you at [Event] - [topic, 2-3 words]
templates.body:
Hi [First name],

Really enjoyed our conversation at [Event] about [the pain they described].

That challenge you mentioned - [restate their words back] - is exactly what we work on: we help [ICP] [outcome + number], and [one proof point].

Would a 20-minute call next week make sense to dig in? Happy to work around your calendar.

Best,
[Founder]

templates.title: The Forwardable Email (intro request, double opt-in)
templates.when: Asking a connector for an intro. The connector forwards instead of composing.
templates.subject: Quick intro request - [Startup] x [Target Company]
templates.body:
Hi [Connector],

Would you be comfortable introducing me to [Name] at [Company]? Feel free to forward the paragraph below, and no worries at all if the timing isn't right.

---
[Startup] helps [ICP] cut [pain metric] by [number]. They're already working with [proof point]. [Founder] would love 20 minutes with [Name] to see whether this is relevant for their team. Worth a look?

templates.title: Recap (within 24 hours of every meeting)
templates.when: Within 24 hours of every meeting. What is not in the recap did not happen.
templates.subject: Recap + next steps - [Startup] / [Company]
templates.body:
Hi [First name], thank you for the time today. Quick recap:
- [Their pain, in their words, with a number]
- [What was agreed or proposed]
- Next step: [the next step, with an owner and a date]

I'll send [what you promised] [when]. Anything I missed?

slots.their_pain: [Their pain, in their words, with a number]
slots.next_step: [the next step, with an owner and a date]

templates.example:
Subject: Recap + next steps - [Startup] / [Company]

Hi Michael, thank you for the time today. Quick recap:
- Your team spends ~15 hrs/week on manual claim triage
- A 2-week pilot scoped to auto-triage could prove value fast
- Next step: intro to Dana from your data team by Friday

I'll send the pilot one-pager tomorrow. Anything I missed?

templates.title: Value bump (day 3-4)
templates.when: Day 3-4 after the meeting, and once per quarter in nurture. Never "just checking in".
templates.body: Hi [First name] - saw [the fresh reason: an article, a metric, a customer, the feature they asked about] and thought of our conversation: [link]. Still happy to [the next step you proposed] - would a quick call next week work?

slots.fresh_reason: [the fresh reason: an article, a metric, a customer, the feature they asked about]

templates.notes: Reply in the same thread, so no new subject line.
templates.example: Hi Michael - saw this new benchmark on claims automation and thought of our conversation: [link]. Still happy to scope that pilot - would a quick call next week work?

templates.title: Second angle (day 8-10; shorter, one closed question)
templates.when: Day 8-10. Shorter than the value bump. One closed question.
templates.body: Hi [First name] - quick one: is [the next step] still on the table for [timeframe], or should I circle back next quarter?
templates.notes: Reply in the same thread, so no new subject line.

templates.title: The Breakup Email (day 15-20; paradoxically the highest reply rate)
templates.when: Day 15-20 with no reply, or as soon as the verdict is Red.
templates.subject: Closing the loop
templates.body: Hi [First name], I haven't heard back, so I'll assume the timing isn't right and close this on my end - no hard feelings at all. If things change, my door is always open. Wishing you and the team a great quarter!

templates.title: Re-entry after the founder went silent (the FOUNDER dropped the thread)
templates.when: The founder dropped the thread. Do not over-apologize; lead with new value and restart the clock.
templates.subject: [New concrete development] - picking this back up
templates.body:
Hi [First name],

Since we last spoke, [the single most impressive new fact: pilot went live, new customer, metric moved].

That made me think of your [pain/initiative] - worth restarting the conversation? Happy to share what we've learned either way.

Best,
[Founder]

slots.new_fact: [the single most impressive new fact: pilot went live, new customer, metric moved]

templates.title: Monthly investor update (how "keep us posted" becomes a term sheet)
templates.when: Monthly-ish to every fund that said "keep us posted", plus current backers. Same 2-3 KPIs every month so slope is visible; one honest setback when real; exactly one ask.
templates.subject: [Startup] update - [Month]: [headline metric or milestone]
templates.body:
Hi [First name],

Quick monthly update:

Shipped: [1-2 product lines]
Sold / Pipeline: [pilot status, logos, revenue or LOI movement - the slope]
Learned: [one honest insight, including a setback if real]
Ask: [one specific ask: an intro, a candidate, feedback on X]

Thanks - happy to go deeper on any of it.

[Founder]

slots.headline: [headline metric or milestone]
slots.sold: [pilot status, logos, revenue or LOI movement - the slope]
slots.learned: [one honest insight, including a setback if real]
slots.ask: [one specific ask: an intro, a candidate, feedback on X]

templates.title: Bar-extraction reply to an investor soft pass
templates.when: Reply to "too early / keep us posted / come back with traction".
templates.body:
Hi [First name],

Completely understand - thanks for the straight read.

So I make the next conversation worth your time: what would you need to see in the next 6 months for this to be a strong yes?

I'll add you to our monthly updates either way. Thanks again for the time.

Best,
[Founder]
templates.notes: The open question here is deliberate: it extracts the bar.

templates.title: Thank-you (within 24h of any favor or intro outcome)
templates.body: Hi [First name] - thank you again for [the specific thing]. [One-line outcome or what you're doing with it.]

slots.outcome: [One-line outcome or what you're doing with it.]

templates.title: Loop-close to the connector who made it happen
templates.when: After the meeting an intro produced. Two lines: what happened, and thank you.
templates.body: Hi [Connector] - quick loop-close: met with [Name], [one-line outcome]. Thank you for making it happen!

templates.title: LinkedIn connection note (max ~250 chars, never a pitch)
templates.when: Connecting on LinkedIn before or after a first touch.
templates.body: Hi [First name] - enjoyed your [talk/post] on [topic] ([one specific detail]). Building in the same space at [Startup]; would love to connect.

templates.title: Scheduling with slots (always in THEIR timezone)
templates.when: Offering times. Always in the recipient's timezone. `playbook.py template --id scheduling --tz ET` fills real dates.
templates.body:
Happy to work around your calendar - would any of these work ([their TZ])?
- Tue [date], 9:00-11:00
- Wed [date], 8:00-10:00
- Thu [date], 13:00-15:00
Or grab any time that suits you here: [scheduling link]

templates.title: First reply to an intro (BCC protocol)
templates.when: The first reply after an intro lands. Within hours, not days. Moves the connector out of the thread.
templates.body:
Thanks [Connector] (moving you to BCC to spare your inbox)!

Hi [Name], [one line on why this is relevant to them]. [Your one easy ask]

slots.name: [Name]
slots.relevance: [one line on why this is relevant to them]

templates.notes: The BCC line is from the guide. The second paragraph is a slot for the founder's own reply.

americanize_prompt.title: The Americanize Prompt (for founders to keep as a shortcut)
americanize_prompt.text:
You are an American business-communication editor working for an Israeli startup founder. Rewrite the email below so it reads like a native American B2B email:
- Max 5 sentences, bottom line up front
- Exactly one ask, phrased as an easy yes/no question
- Warm-professional tone with natural softeners ("Would you be open to...", "No worries if not")
- No bluntness, no unnecessary technical depth (that belongs in the meeting)
- Keep all facts intact. Flag anything that sounds pushy or too direct in American business culture.
Return only: a one-line subject suggestion + the rewritten email.

[PASTE YOUR EMAIL HERE]
